figures.finding: A resident pays nothing on the first RM5,000 of chargeable income, then 1%, 3%, 6%, 11%, 19%, 25%, 26%, 28% and 30% above RM2,000,000, after a personal relief of RM9,000 (in force since YA 2010); there is no local income tax. Budget 2027 proposes, from YA 2027, 18% on RM70,001–100,000, a new 24% band to RM150,000, 28% only to RM1,000,000 and 30% above, and a RM12,000 relief.

proposedFromYA2027.status: Budget 2027 proposal (Finance Bill), not yet law

figures.applies: Resident individuals, YA 2026 (the scale the Ministry of Finance gives as current in its Budget 2027 tax measures); the YA 2027 changes are proposals.

sources.said: Kadar cukai pendapatan bagi individu pemastautin adalah progresif di antara 0% dan 30% seperti berikut: … 0 – 5,000 0 5,001 – 20,000 1 20,001 – 35,000 3 35,001 – 50,000 6 50,001 – 70,000 11 70,001 – 100,000 19 100,001 – 400,000 25 400,001 – 600,000 26 600,001 – 2,000,000 28 Melebihi 2,000,000 30 … Mulai tahun taksiran 2010, pelepasan cukai pendapatan individu ke atas individu dan saudara tanggungan dinaikkan daripada RM8,000 kepada RM9,000. … dicadangkan pelepasan cukai pendapatan ke atas individu dan saudara tanggungan dinaikkan daripada RM9,000 kepada RM12,000. … Mulai tahun taksiran 2027.

figures.finding: EPF takes 11% from a Malaysian employee under 60, with the employer paying 13% on wages to RM5,000 and 12% above; non-citizens pay 2% each; SOCSO employment-injury and invalidity contributions are capped at RM29.75 a month for the employee and RM104.15 for the employer.

sources.said: Category Wages % of contribution of employee’s wages (minimum) Below 60 years old Age 60 and above Malaysian ≤ M YR 5,000 Employer: 13% Employee: 11% Employer: 4% Employee: 0% > MYR 5,000 Employer: 12% Employee: 11% … Non-Malaysians No limit Employer: 2% Employee: 2% … The sum is based on the employee’s monthly wages and is restricted to a maximum of MYR 104.15 for the employer and MYR 29.75 for the employee.

figures.finding: A non-resident public entertainer's gross income for services in Malaysia, including fees, prize money and paid benefits, bears 15% withholding under section 109A; a non-resident individual is otherwise taxed at a flat 30%.

value.base: gross income including fees, allowances and reimbursed benefits

figures.applies: Non-resident public entertainers (stage, radio or television artistes, musicians and the like)

sources.said: gross income which is subject to WHT under S109A. Such payments include fees, prize money, allowances as well as reimbursements for benefits like accommodation, meals and airfare. … 8 Tax Rate on Income of NRPE The rate of tax is 15% on gross income under Schedule 1, Part II of the ITA.
A non-resident individual is taxed at a flat rate of 30% on total taxable income.

figures.finding: Malaysia has no VAT; service tax is 8% on listed taxable services (6% on food and beverage, telecoms, parking and logistics), and a provider must register once its taxable services exceed RM500,000 in 12 months (RM1,500,000 for food and beverage).
figures.applies: 2026. The RM500,000 threshold is PwC's table (its row labels are not in the page text); whether a performer's or writer's fee is a listed taxable service is not settled (see blocker).

sources.said: What is the rate of tax for service tax? i. The tax rate is 8% for all taxable services except; … ii. F&B, Logistics, Telecommunications, and Parking are at a rate of 6%. … The backward method is based on the value of taxable services for any month, combined with the value of taxable services for the 11 months preceding that month.

Sales tax is generally an ad valorem tax. The ad valorem rates are 5% or 10% depending on the class of goods. The rate of service tax is 8% for all taxable services except for the following, which are at 6%: Provision of food and beverage services. Telecommunication services. Parking services. Logistics services.
A person is liable to be registered if the total value of his taxable services for a 12-month period exceeds or is expected to exceed the prescribed registration threshold.

figures.finding: The year of assessment is the calendar year; the return is due by 30 April without business income and by 30 June with it.

sources.said: The Malaysian tax year is the calendar year (i.e. 1 January to 31 December).
The tax return is submitted not later than 30 April (without business income) and 30 June (with business income) in the following calendar year.
